item.title: Gambling Goblin SEO abuse, DKIM-signed Reply-To diversion, and AI medical device pentesting
item.content:encoded:
Window: 02 Sep 10:00 → 02 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Gaming the system: how a Chinese-speaking actor turned Brazilian government sites into an SEO weapon — Must Read

Check Point Research says a Chinese-speaking cybercrime group linked to Earth Berberoka is compromising Brazilian government and education web servers, installing malicious Apache modules that turn trusted domains into stealth proxies for gambling-themed fake app-store pages and SEO manipulation. The same scalable infrastructure and Linux malware toolkit could be quickly repurposed from search fraud to direct malware delivery.

  • Check Point Research tracked a sustained campaign since mid-2025 against Brazilian organizations, primarily government and educational institutions, by a Chinese-speaking cybercrime cluster it calls Gambling Goblin.
  • The attackers install malicious Apache modules on compromised web servers to reverse-proxy selected visitors to attacker-controlled phishing pages while the traffic appears to come from the legitimate domain.
  • The phishing pages impersonate trusted app-distribution platforms such as Google Play, Microsoft Store, and Amazon while promoting online gambling and sports betting to Brazilian users.
  • The group deploys a heavily obfuscated Linux toolkit that includes DownPro, AlphaAgent, oRAT, a 3snake-based credential stealer, an SSH brute-forcer, and reconnaissance tools.
  • Check Point Research found related phishing networks localized in Vietnamese, Spanish, and English, as well as infrastructure that generates fresh domains daily.

Technologies: web-server, proxy, remote-access, cloud-platform

Products: apache-http-server, google-play, microsoft-store, amazon-appstore, bing, grpc

Vendors: apache-software-foundation, google, microsoft, amazon, cloudflare

Fully Signed, Fully Passed: The Reply-To Was the Payload — Should Read

A genuine European government mailbox sent a fully authenticated phishing email whose only payload was a hidden Reply-To diversion to an attacker-controlled address. Because DKIM, DMARC, and ARC all passed, the key lesson is that email authentication proves origin and integrity, not whether the reply path is safe.

  • A senior executive at a professional certification and credentialing organization received a one-line RFQ follow-up email from a genuine mailbox at a European regional government body.
  • The message had no link or attachment and used a Reply-To field containing both an attacker-controlled address, infodesk@frontdesk-investment[.]com, and the genuine government mailbox.
  • The government domain’s valid DKIM signature explicitly covered the Reply-To header, showing the covert reply address was present before the sending organization’s outbound gateway signed the message.
  • The email passed DKIM twice, DMARC, ARC, and Microsoft’s composite authentication verdict, demonstrating that the message was not forged even though its reply path was redirected.
  • The article says the practical control is to surface reply-path divergence during triage, especially when an inbound message’s reply domain does not match the From domain or contains multiple reply addresses.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis, microsoft-365

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft

When Everyone Can Find Your Bugs: Medical Device Security After AI — Optional

Health-ISAC and ELTON Cyber are offering an on-demand webinar on how AI-driven pentesting is dramatically increasing medical device vulnerability findings, creating new triage and evidence requirements for manufacturers under FDA expectations.

  • Health-ISAC and ELTON Medical Device AI-Pentesting discuss how AI has collapsed the cost of vulnerability discovery to nearly zero.
  • The article says manufacturers now face more findings per product and per release than any team can triage by hand.
  • Each finding requires an evidence-based disposition under FDA premarket 524B and postmarket expectations.
  • ELTON, a company specializing in AI pentesting and vulnerability management for medical devices, shares its pipeline and solution in the webinar.
  • The discussion covers the OpenAI and HuggingFace incident as an example of the transformative power of AI pentesting.

Vendors: elton-cyber, openai, hugging-face

item.title: ExfilSquad UK Extortion, EU Machinery Cyber Rules, and AI Data Policy Gaps
item.content:encoded:
Window: 02 Sep 06:00 → 02 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

UK Cybercrime Journal: ExfilSquad Emerges — Must Read

ExfilSquad is targeting UK public sector, education, and law enforcement organizations with data-theft-only extortion, exploiting exposed SaaS, CRM, and Microsoft Power Pages configurations rather than deploying ransomware. The key risk is that misconfigured cloud-facing business portals can leak large volumes of sensitive contact and administrative data, which the group then distributes via torrents to increase pressure on victims.

  • In mid-2026, the cybercriminal group ExfilSquad launched an extortion campaign targeting prominent UK organizations across the public sector, education, and law enforcement, as well as other firms worldwide.
  • ExfilSquad operates as a pure data extortion group that steals data and threatens to publish it on its onion-based Data Leak Site if a ransom is not paid, rather than deploying encryptors or destructive malware.
  • The UK Department for Education, the Police National Legal Database, and Newcastle University confirmed breaches linked to ExfilSquad involving hundreds of thousands of records and, in the PNLD case, data affecting over 100,000 police officers, staff, and criminal justice professionals.
  • Analysis of ExfilSquad’s leak site details indicated that its primary attack vector involves exploiting misconfigurations in cloud portals, CRM platforms, internal case management systems, and publicly accessible Microsoft Power Pages data tables.
  • ExfilSquad uploaded multi-gigabyte torrent files for each victim to its TOR leak site and assigned distinct Torrent Trackers and initial Web Seeds per victim.

Technologies: cloud-platform, database

Products: microsoft-power-pages, salesforce, snowflake, salesloft

Vendors: microsoft, salesforce, snowflake, salesloft

Policy on Paper, Risk in Practice — Optional

Most organizations have AI data security policies, but fewer than one in 10 can enforce them consistently in real time across AI tools. The key risk is that sensitive data now moves through prompts, copy-paste, and AI-generated outputs faster than traditional file-based controls can track or block.

  • Nearly half of surveyed organizations still rely on written policies, post-event monitoring, or inconsistently enforced controls as their primary approach to data security enforcement.
  • Only 11% of organizations enforce data protection policies in real time across most environments, and only 8% do so for AI tools specifically.
  • Although 67% of organizations maintain a formal AI policy, fewer than one in 10 enforce it consistently in AI environments.
  • Most data protection architectures were built for files, while sensitive information increasingly moves through prompts, AI-generated summaries, and copy-pasted excerpts.
  • Only one in five organizations can apply consistent policy to prompt and text submissions into AI tools, and fewer than one in ten can recognize sensitive data once it has been modified, reformatted, or partially copied.

Technologies: dlp

Products: netskope-one-data-security, netskope-one-ai-security, zero-trust-engine, dlp-on-demand, claude-enterprise

Vendors: netskope, anthropic

item.title: CVE-2026-6471 Enables PostgreSQL Replication Accounts to Execute Arbitrary Code
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Sep 22:00 → 02 Sep 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

PostGREShell: The database powering much of the internet had an open door for 12 years — Must Read

Cyera researchers found a critical PostgreSQL flaw, CVE-2026-6471, that lets low-privilege replication accounts load arbitrary plugins and gain remote code execution, superuser access, and persistence. Organizations should patch immediately, audit replication accounts, and restrict replication access and outbound SMB/NFS traffic.

  • Cyera Research discovered CVE-2026-6471, a critical PostgreSQL vulnerability affecting every PostgreSQL version from 9.4 through 18.
  • The flaw lets an account with the REPLICATION attribute load and execute arbitrary code through the logical replication output plugin path because the plugin name is passed to the loader without validation.
  • On Windows, an attacker can exploit the issue remotely by using a UNC path over SMB so PostgreSQL loads a DLL from the attacker’s server without placing a file on the target system.
  • After code execution, the attacker can escalate to PostgreSQL superuser by calling internal functions and directly modifying pg_authid, bypassing normal SQL permission checks.
  • The article recommends applying the PostgreSQL security update, auditing REPLICATION accounts, restricting replication access in pg_hba.conf, and blocking outbound SMB and NFS from database servers.

Technologies: database

Products: postgresql, amazon-rds, azure-database-for-postgresql, google-cloud-sql, supabase, neon

Vendors: postgresql-global-development-group, cyera, amazon-web-services, microsoft, google-cloud, supabase, neon

item.title: Healthcare Sharing, UK OT Proof, Snowflake Controls, and Self-Spoofed Phishing
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Sep 10:00 → 01 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Email From Yourself That Your Own Domain Disowned — May Read

A phishing email spoofed a financial advisor’s own address and reached the inbox despite SPF, DKIM, and DMARC failures because enforcement and composite authentication did not block it. The lure used a legitimate monday.com tracking link to redirect to a disposable credential-harvesting page, highlighting the need to flag self-addressed spoofing and inspect final link destinations.

  • A client-facing financial advisor received a document-signature phishing email whose From and To headers were both the advisor’s own work address.
  • The email arrived from commodity bulk-hosting infrastructure, explicitly failed SPF, had no DKIM signature, failed DMARC, yet Microsoft composite authentication returned a pass.
  • The “Start signing” button routed through a legitimate monday.com link-tracking hostname whose embedded token decoded to a disposable credential-harvesting page on sharedfile.realestatecotblrp.vu.
  • IRONSCALES Themis scored the message at 90% confidence and labeled it credential theft based on the suspicious link and the sender pattern of an external sender using an internal-looking self-addressed email.
  • The article recommends alerting on inbound mail where the From address matches the receiving mailbox, enforcing DMARC, watching for disagreement between authentication results, and resolving vendor link trackers before trusting them.

Technologies: email-security

Products: monday-com-link-tracker, themis, ironscales-adaptive-ai

Vendors: microsoft, monday-com, ironscales, colocrossing

What the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill’s New Standard of Proof Means for OT Organisations — Optional

The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill would push OT organisations from periodic compliance evidence to continuous, defensible proof that they know their assets, risks, ownership, and changes in real time. Many OT environments lack that live visibility today, so boards should close the gap before regulators or incidents force the issue.

  • The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, as currently drafted, introduces a requirement for organisations to show ongoing proof that they manage cyber risk in their plants rather than relying on reasonable periodic effort.
  • The article says policies, point-in-time audits, named risk owners, and older penetration test reports will not be enough to answer regulator questions about what is connected to the network today, what has changed, or what current risk looks like.
  • OT environments are described as harder to manage continuously than IT environments because they often accumulate equipment over decades, include vendor-installed remote access, and have network changes made to maintain operations without formal records.
  • A defensible response requires a current asset inventory, risk scoring tied to operational function, mapping to a recognised methodology such as IEC 62443’s zone and conduit model, and clear ownership with a defined review cadence.
  • The article argues that many boards have not yet tested the gap between believing OT risk is managed and being able to prove it, and that closing this gap before a regulatory conversation is stronger than doing so during one.

Technologies: ics-scada, plc, network-monitoring, remote-access

Vendors: radiflow

Collaborating for a Safer Ecosystem: Information Sharing and Public-Private Partnerships — Optional

The article argues that the Boston Scientific cyberattack shows healthcare cybersecurity cannot be handled by any single organization alone. Stronger information sharing and public-private partnerships are needed so threat intelligence and lessons learned can help the whole sector defend faster.

  • The article argues that a resilient healthcare ecosystem requires collaboration among medical device manufacturers, healthcare providers, government agencies, and cybersecurity vendors.
  • The article states that sharing threat intelligence, best practices, and lessons learned from incidents can help the healthcare industry raise its collective defense.
  • The article says public-private partnerships are crucial for developing standards, conducting research, and providing resources.
  • The article states that Health-ISAC plays a vital role in facilitating the exchange of information.

item.title: Mirage Kitten Deploys NodeRabbit and PollCat RATs Against MEA Aviation and FinTech
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Sep 06:00 → 01 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Mirage Kitten targeting aviation and FinTech sectors across the Middle East and Africa with a new malware set — Must Read

Kaspersky reports that Mirage Kitten is targeting aviation and fintech organizations in the Middle East and Africa with new cross-platform Node.js/JavaScript RATs called NodeRabbit and PollCat, delivered through fake recruiter coding challenges. The campaign marks a shift in the group’s tooling while continuing its use of LinkedIn lures, cloud-hosted infrastructure, and developer-focused social engineering.

  • Kaspersky uncovered two previously undocumented cross-platform RAT families, NodeRabbit and PollCat, during monitoring of Mirage Kitten activity.
  • Mirage Kitten delivered NodeRabbit and PollCat through spear-phishing messages on LinkedIn and other job search platforms that contained trojanized coding challenge archives.
  • NodeRabbit is built with Node.js, targets Windows, Linux, and macOS, and was observed in variants on systems in Afghanistan, Egypt, and Ethiopia.
  • PollCat is written in obfuscated JavaScript, starts during the fake React coding challenge application startup, and can continue running even if the user fails OTP validation.
  • Kaspersky attributes the activity to Mirage Kitten with high confidence based on malware similarities to Retrograde/MiniFast, victimology, lure-hosting tradecraft, and infrastructure patterns.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, package-registry, source-control, operating-system, proxy, remote-access

item.title: Anubis Hits Fairlife; pnpm 12 Rust Rewrite Adds Supply Chain Controls
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Sep 02:00 → 01 Sep 06:00 UTC (4 hours)

From a Stolen Login to a Ransomware Leak Site: What Our Telemetry Shows About the Path Threat Actors Take — Should Read

Constella links Fairlife’s public Anubis ransomware leak to a broader pattern where stolen credentials from infostealer-infected vendor laptops can give attackers access to corporate CMS, cloud, SSO, and internal systems. The key takeaway is that third-party credential exposure, including cookies and browser autofill data, must be monitored as seriously as a company’s own endpoints because it can become the first step toward ransomware.

  • Anubis added Fairlife, a dairy brand owned by The Coca-Cola Company, to its dark web extortion portal, and Coca-Cola publicly confirmed the ransomware incident.
  • Anubis claimed it exfiltrated close to a terabyte of internal data and used an optional wipe mode against part of the victim’s virtualization infrastructure.
  • The leaked data was organized into engineering and OT documentation, production and formulation data, and HR and people data.
  • Constella analyzed a separate credential package believed to belong to a third-party digital agency employee that contained 789 saved credential pairs, 540 browser session cookies, and a local password manager vault store.
  • The credential package included hundreds of credentials for brand site content management environments, plus credentials for cloud infrastructure, DevOps, source control, corporate identity, and SSO providers.

Technologies: cms, cloud-platform

Products: hunter-plus, adobe-experience-manager, crxde-lite, package-manager, amazon-web-services, slack

Vendors: constella, adobe, amazon-web-services, slack

pnpm 12’s Rust Rewrite Cuts Install Times by Up to 90% — May Read

pnpm 12 is now stable with a Rust rewrite that keeps pnpm 11 compatibility while delivering major install-time and storage improvements in early real-world testing. Its maintainers have narrowed public benchmark claims after flawed cross-package-manager comparisons, emphasizing faster pnpm performance rather than claiming overall market leadership.

  • pnpm 12 is now stable and replaces pnpm’s Node.js and TypeScript foundation with a Rust rewrite while preserving the commands, settings, and lockfile format used by pnpm 11.
  • In Vercel’s 21-project Turborepo workspace, pnpm 12 reduced median install times by 64.4% to 90.5% compared with pnpm 10.28 across six tested scenarios.
  • pnpm removed Bun and Yarn from the comparison displayed on its benchmark page after bugs made published cross-tool package manager rankings unreliable.
  • pnpm 12 adds supply chain security-related features including project-aware global bins, direct package manager provisioning, registry revisions, signed remote build artifacts, and deterministic cyclic lockfiles.
  • The upgrade has behavioral changes that may affect workflows, including removal of `pnpm install --resolution-only`, canonical HTTPS resolution for Git dependencies on GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket, and warnings for unknown settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

Technologies: source-control

Products: pnpm, pnpm-12, pnpm-11, turborepo, bun, yarn, npm, corepack, node.js, deno, vlt-benchmark-suite, pnpr, github, gitlab, bitbucket

Vendors: pnpm, vercel, bun, yarn, npm, nodejs, deno, vlt, github, gitlab, bitbucket

Microsoft Teams Notifications Are Now Available in Socket — Optional

Socket now supports Microsoft Teams notifications, letting security and engineering teams route filtered supply chain alerts and attack campaign updates directly into Teams channels. Notifications use Adaptive Cards with severity summaries, affected repositories, previews, and links back to the Socket dashboard.

  • Socket has added Microsoft Teams as a notification channel for organization alerts and supply chain attack campaign notifications.
  • Owners and Admins can connect a Microsoft Teams channel in Settings → Integrations → Notifications using a Microsoft Workflows incoming webhook.
  • Notification subscriptions can route alerts based on event type, category, severity, Socket priority, repository, package ecosystem, and affected repository.
  • Socket sends Microsoft Teams notifications as Adaptive Cards that include severity totals, affected repository counts, previews of findings, and links back to the Socket dashboard.
  • Microsoft Teams notifications are available now on Socket Team, Business, and Enterprise plans.

Products: socket, microsoft-teams, microsoft-workflows, adaptive-cards

Vendors: socket, microsoft

AI Agents Are Changing Ransomware Attacks on Healthcare Organizations — Optional

AI agents could make ransomware against healthcare organizations faster, more scalable, and harder to contain by autonomously carrying out complex attack steps like exploitation, credential theft, and lateral movement. Real-time threat intelligence sharing will be critical to disrupting these campaigns before they spread.

  • Generative AI has made familiar forms of cybercrime faster, cheaper, and easier to scale in the past few years.
  • Attackers use generative AI for reconnaissance, vulnerability research, drafting convincing phishing emails, and generating malicious code quickly.
  • The article describes AI agents as systems capable of autonomously executing complex attack sequences with minimal or no human oversight.
  • A recent OpenAI test model incident showed an AI system chaining together exploitation, credential theft, privilege escalation, and lateral movement with limited human direction while normal production safety measures were disabled.
  • The article argues that real-time cyber threat intelligence sharing will help organizations disrupt ransomware campaigns before they spread across the healthcare ecosystem.

Vendors: openai

The dark figure of supply chain detection — Optional

The article argues that supply-chain detection must go beyond cheap string and IOC rules because those only catch already-seen attackers. Durable detection requires behavioral baselines for normal package activity so anomalous install-time execution, credential access, payload staging, and exfiltration can expose sophisticated malicious packages even when indicators are new or obfuscated.

  • The article argues that string-level detection rules only catch attackers who reuse artifacts that defenders have already seen, while behavioral rules are the main way to detect unknown malicious packages.
  • The article says effective behavioral detection requires a clear baseline of what normal package behavior looks like, because unexpected actions only stand out when normal behavior has been mapped.
  • The article recommends a portfolio of detection rules across an adapted Pyramid of Pain, with cheap string and indicator rules handling high-volume reused threats and higher-tier behavioral rules targeting more sophisticated attackers.
  • The article states that normal package behavior should be mapped by package type because a build tool may legitimately spawn child processes or touch the filesystem during installation, while a small string-formatting helper doing the same would be suspicious.
  • Aikido Security flagged a newly published version of Keyv on August 4, 2026 after it executed heavily obfuscated JavaScript during installation, downloaded Bun, and executed another obfuscated JavaScript file.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control

Products: aikido-intel, keyv, npm, github, pypi, nuget, bun

Vendors: aikido-security, npm, github, python-software-foundation, microsoft, keyv, oven-sh

What the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill’s New Standard of Proof Means for OT Organisations — Optional

The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill would push OT organisations from periodic compliance evidence to continuous, defensible proof that they know their assets, risks, ownership, and changes in real time. Many OT environments lack that live visibility today, so boards should close the gap before regulators or incidents force the issue.

  • The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, as currently drafted, introduces a requirement for organisations to show ongoing proof that they manage cyber risk in their plants rather than relying on reasonable periodic effort.
  • The article says policies, point-in-time audits, named risk owners, and older penetration test reports will not be enough to answer regulator questions about what is connected to the network today, what has changed, or what current risk looks like.
  • OT environments are described as harder to manage continuously than IT environments because they often accumulate equipment over decades, include vendor-installed remote access, and have network changes made to maintain operations without formal records.
  • A defensible response requires a current asset inventory, risk scoring tied to operational function, mapping to a recognised methodology such as IEC 62443’s zone and conduit model, and clear ownership with a defined review cadence.
  • The article argues that many boards have not yet tested the gap between believing OT risk is managed and being able to prove it, and that closing this gap before a regulatory conversation is stronger than doing so during one.

Technologies: ics-scada, plc, network-monitoring, remote-access

Vendors: radiflow

From Metrics to Meaning: Transforming Medical Device Cybersecurity into a Strategic Risk Narrative — Optional

Health-ISAC’s white paper argues that medical device manufacturers need to turn cybersecurity metrics into a clear risk narrative that links technical activity to patient safety, regulatory exposure, product resilience, and executive decision-making.

  • The paper says medical device manufacturers are generally proficient at generating cybersecurity data from sources such as product SBOMs, vulnerability management platforms, quality system actions, and regulatory process actions.
  • The article states that many organizations struggle to translate cybersecurity data into a clear story about risk, security posture, and business impact.
  • The paper presents a practical approach for transforming cybersecurity metrics into a structured risk narrative for medical device manufacturers.
  • The article says the goal is to help organizations identify the metrics that matter, connect operational measurements to executive decision-making, and show how product security efforts reduce risk, protect patients, and build trust.
  • The article argues that cybersecurity metrics are most valuable when they explain how an organization is managing risk, improving resilience, and earning the confidence of regulators, customers, and patients.

Vendors: health-isac

Collaborating for a Safer Ecosystem: Information Sharing and Public-Private Partnerships — Optional

The article argues that the Boston Scientific cyberattack shows healthcare cybersecurity cannot be handled by any single organization. It emphasizes rapid threat intelligence sharing and public-private partnerships, including groups like Health-ISAC, as essential to strengthening collective defenses.

  • The article says the Boston Scientific cyberattack highlights that no single entity can tackle the cybersecurity challenge alone.
  • The article argues that a resilient healthcare ecosystem requires collaboration among medical device manufacturers, healthcare providers, government agencies, and cybersecurity vendors.
  • The article states that sharing threat intelligence, best practices, and lessons learned from incidents can help the healthcare industry improve its collective defenses.
  • The article says public-private partnerships are important for developing standards, conducting research, and providing resources.
  • The article identifies Health-ISAC as playing a vital role in facilitating information sharing across the healthcare sector.

Vendors: boston-scientific, health-isac

Top DSPM tools in 2026 — Optional

The article argues that code-based DSPM is better for fixing data exposure at the source because it traces sensitive data through application code without accessing production data, while storage-based tools mainly find where sensitive data already exists. It positions Aikido Security as the top choice for this approach, with Wiz, Cyera, Varonis, and Orca better suited to data inventory and cloud or access-context use cases.

  • The article says DSPM tools help companies map where sensitive data is stored and exposed, including personal data, payment details, health records, secrets, tokens, and data sent into AI features.
  • The article distinguishes storage-based DSPM tools, which connect to databases, buckets, and warehouses to read data, from code-based DSPM tools, which read application code to trace how sensitive fields move without touching production data.
  • The article presents Aikido Security as its preferred tool for finding and fixing data exposure at the source because it identifies exact files and lines and can open pull requests for code-level fixes.
  • The article says Wiz and Orca provide DSPM as modules inside broader cloud security platforms, while Cyera and Varonis are described as more dedicated data security platforms.
  • The article states that code-based DSPM can catch risky logging, over-broad API responses, third-party sharing, weak storage, and incomplete deletion before data reaches production, while storage-based tools are stronger at finding forgotten or orphaned data already sitting in stores.

Technologies: dlp

Products: aikido-dspm, wiz-dspm, cyera-dspm, varonis-data-security-platform, orca-cloud-security-platform

Vendors: aikido-security, wiz, cyera, varonis, orca-security

Acronis Cyberthreats Update, August 2026 — Optional

Acronis reports that ShinyHunters breached a third-party IT service management platform used by EY’s tax practice and stole client tax, personal, and financial documents, highlighting the growing risk of SaaS and DevOps supply-chain access. July malware detections declined for the third straight month, but remained above early-2026 levels.

  • In July 2026, Ernst & Young confirmed a data breach after the ShinyHunters extortion gang added the firm to its dark web leak site on July 27.
  • EY found that an unauthorized party accessed a third-party IT service management platform used by its tax practice between March 28 and April 12, 2026, and downloaded documents belonging to several EY clients.
  • ShinyHunters told BleepingComputer it did not breach EY’s own infrastructure directly, but obtained credentials through a supply-chain compromise that gave it reach into EY’s Jira, GitHub and Azure environments.
  • The stolen data included documents containing client tax information, personal information, and financial information used to prepare client tax filings.
  • Acronis reported that the percentage of unique clients with at least one malware threat blocked at the endpoint decreased to 5.6% in July 2026, down from 6% in June.

Technologies: source-control, cloud-platform, xdr, antivirus, email-security, dlp, backup

Products: jira, github, microsoft-azure, acronis-cyber-protect-cloud, acronis-genai-protection, acronis-xdr

Vendors: atlassian, github, microsoft, acronis

Varonis Achieves Snowflake Premier Partner Tier and Is Now Available on Snowflake Marketplace — Optional

Varonis announced it has reached Snowflake Premier Partner status and is now available on the Snowflake Marketplace, making it easier for Snowflake customers to buy and deploy Varonis for data security. The integration helps organizations discover sensitive Snowflake data, map access permissions, and detect risky behavior while supporting analytics and AI initiatives.

  • Snowflake customers can find Varonis on the Snowflake Marketplace and apply a portion of their committed capacity to Varonis through the Snowflake Marketplace Capacity Drawdown program.

  • Varonis maps effective permissions for every user and uses behavioral baselines to detect risky access patterns involving users, systems, or AI systems.

The Prioritization Problem: Why More Findings Don’t Mean Less Risk — Optional

Bishop Fox’s on-demand webinar argues that more security findings don’t automatically reduce risk, and that teams need Continuous Threat Exposure Management to validate what attackers can actually exploit. The key takeaway is to prioritize exploitable, real-world exposures over raw vulnerability volume.

  • Bishop Fox experts discuss why security teams have more visibility than ever but still struggle to identify what actually matters.
  • The on-demand webinar focuses on Continuous Threat Exposure Management and how Bishop Fox’s Cosmos team helps organizations cut through security noise.
  • The article says effective prioritization requires validating what attackers can actually exploit rather than simply collecting more data.
  • The conversation covers how offensive security testing can help separate exploitable risk from background noise.

So Your CFO's Phone Has Been Pwned: A DFIR Journey — Optional

When a CFO’s phone is suspected of compromise, a single IOC like an IP address should be treated as the start of a broader DFIR investigation, not the incident itself. Historical infrastructure data from tools like Censys can reveal malware panels, exploit chains, related hosts, and rotating attacker infrastructure needed to scope exposure and improve detections.

  • The article presents two fictional mobile incident response scenarios involving a CFO’s phone, one using Android malware resembling ERMAC or HookBot and one involving an iPhone connection to DarkSword infrastructure.
  • In the Android scenario, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint detects a sideloaded malicious APK called “Chrome Update,” prompting actions such as blocking the device from corporate resources, revoking sessions, preserving the phone, and reviewing accessible credentials.
  • Censys ARC observed the Android-related host 118.107.45[.]29 carrying a HookBot threat label from mid-July through August 13, 2026, and later changes matched HookBot’s IP-whitelist security gate behavior.
  • In the iPhone scenario, Zscaler web logs show the managed iPhone connected to 103.106.190[.]217, which Censys ARC observed serving an Apple ID credential-harvesting page alongside DarkSword iOS exploit-chain infrastructure.
  • The article emphasizes that an IP address, domain, certificate, or hash is evidence of a larger infrastructure picture, and that historical Internet data can help responders scope related hosts, prior activity, and future detections.
